questions.question: Which type of area is this property located in?
questions.description:
📍 Property Area Type
The surrounding area helps determine which lenders can finance the property.
💡 Tip: Choose the option that best matches how the area looks and is commonly described.

options.label: Planned / Development Authority Area
options.helperText: approved layout, township, large housing society

options.label: Converted Land / Approved Residential Use
options.helperText: earlier agricultural or village land, now residential

options.label: Old Municipal Area / Traditional Mohalla
options.helperText: inside city limits, older houses, narrow streets

options.label: Not sure
options.helperText: I'm not certain about the area classification

questions.question: Does the property fall under any special restricted zone?
questions.description:
⛔ Special Restricted Zone
Some zones have additional restrictions that affect which lenders can process the application.

options.label: Cantonment Board area
options.helperText: Military/defense area with special building rules

condition.then: Properties in tribal/Schedule V areas have severe transfer restrictions. Most banks will not finance. Specialized NBFCs may consider at higher rates.
Coastal Regulation Zone properties face construction restrictions. Only CRZ-II (developed urban coastal) is generally financeable with proper environmental clearances.
Cantonment Board properties require additional clearances from the Board. Most banks accept but processing takes longer.
Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) is not applicable in this state. Please verify the property location is actually in a coastal state.
Cantonment Board areas are not present in this state. Please verify the property location.
Tribal / Schedule V areas are not present in this state. Please verify the property location.

questions.question: What category of property is being offered as collateral?
questions.description:
🏢 Property Category
Residential properties get the best LAP terms (60-70% LTV). Commercial (50-60%) and industrial (40-55%) have lower LTV and fewer lender options.

questions.question: What type of construction is it?

condition.then: Very few lenders offer LAP on vacant plots. Expect limited options and lower LTV (40-50%).

questions.question: What is the type of ownership for this property?
questions.description:
📜 Ownership Type
Freehold properties get better loan terms. Leasehold with less than 20 years remaining is nearly impossible to finance.

questions.question: How many years are remaining on the lease?

condition.then: Leasehold properties with less than 20 years remaining are extremely difficult to finance. Most banks will reject.

questions.question: How old is this property?
questions.description:
🏠 Property Age
The age of the property affects loan eligibility, maximum tenure, and valuation.

uiMeta.placeholder: Enter carpet area in sq ft

questions.question: What is the carpet area / plot area? (in sq ft)
questions.description:
📏 Carpet / Plot Area
For constructed properties, enter carpet area (usable floor area). For plots, enter total plot area. Primary metric for valuation.

condition.then: Carpet area seems too low. Please enter the area in square feet.
Please enter a valid carpet area in square feet.

uiMeta.placeholder: Enter built-up area in sq ft

questions.question: Built-up area (in sq ft, if known)
Is the property built as per the development authority’s sanctioned building plan?
questions.description:
🏛️ Property Compliance — Planned Area
In planned/authority areas, lenders check whether construction follows the approved layout and sanctioned plan from DDA/MHADA/BDA/HUDA or similar authority.
💡 Tip: Not fully compliant does not mean rejection — some NBFCs fund deviated properties at different terms.

options.label: Yes — fully as per approved plan
Minor deviations from approved plan
options.helperText: Small differences like balcony enclosure, staircase variation

options.label: Major deviations or no approved plan

condition.then: Properties with deviations from approved plan have fewer lender options. Select NBFCs may still process at adjusted terms.

questions.question: Has the land been formally converted from agricultural to residential use (NA conversion)?
questions.description:
🏛️ Property Compliance — Converted Land
Banks require confirmed NA (Non-Agricultural) conversion before financing any property on converted land. Without this, the property is treated as agricultural — which no bank will finance.

options.label: Yes — NA order received and registered

condition.then: NA conversion is still pending -- loan processing will be on hold until conversion is complete. High-risk status for lenders.
Non-NA land -- ineligible for financing. The land must be converted from agricultural use before any lender can process this loan.

questions.question: Is the property within municipal limits with valid municipal records?
questions.description:
🏛️ Property Compliance — Municipal Area
For properties in old municipal/city areas, lenders verify municipal records, property tax, and building permission history.

options.label: Yes — proper municipal records and building permission
Municipal area but original plan has deviations
options.helperText: Extra floor, balcony extension, unauthorized room addition

options.label: No formal building permission or municipal records

condition.then: Minor deviations in municipal areas are common. Some banks and most NBFCs can still process with adjusted valuation.

questions.question: Is the colony officially recognised or regularized by the government?
questions.description:
🏛️ Property Compliance — Local Colony
Properties in village/panchayat areas are evaluated based on whether the colony or layout has been officially recognized. Regularized colonies have more lender options.

options.label: Yes — colony is regularized with proper records

condition.then: Non-regularized colony properties are not accepted by banks. Specialized housing finance companies (Aavas, Grihashakti) may consider at higher interest rates and lower loan-to-value ratios.

questions.question: Is the property in a government-authorized area and built as per approved plan?
questions.description:
🏛️ Property Compliance Status
This determines which lenders (banks vs NBFCs) can process the application.
💡 Tip: Not fully compliant does not mean rejection — some NBFCs fund non-authorized or deviated properties at different terms.

options.label: Yes — authorized area, as per approved plan
Authorized area, but not as per plan

condition.then: Properties that are not fully compliant may still be eligible for funding through select NBFCs. Fewer lenders will appear in the results, but options are available.

questions.question: Has the building received its OC (Occupancy Certificate) / CC (Completion Certificate)?
questions.description:
📋 OC / CC Status
Most banks require OC/CC for processing. Without OC, lenders may consider the property legally incomplete.

questions.question: Was the house built with a sanctioned building plan from the local authority?
questions.description:
🏛️ Building Plan Approval
For independent houses, lenders check whether construction followed a plan sanctioned by the local authority.

questions.question: Is the property / project RERA registered?
questions.description:
🏢 RERA Registration
RERA registration is mandatory for projects over 500 sq.m. Banks verify RERA number before sanctioning loans for under-construction properties.

condition.then: Banks will not finance under-construction projects without RERA registration. Verify with the builder.

questions.question: What is the current status of the NA (Non-Agricultural) conversion order?
questions.description:
📜 NA Conversion Status
The NA order from the District Collector’s office is the key document proving land use has been changed from agricultural to residential.

options.label: Already in residential zone (no conversion needed)

condition.then: Without NA conversion, no lender can process this loan. The conversion process typically takes 2-6 months.

questions.question: What is the zone classification of this land?
questions.description:
🗺️ Zone Classification
Zone classification determines permissible construction type. Lenders prefer residential or mixed-use zones.

condition.then: Commercial-zoned property: Some lenders may restrict residential loans on commercial-zoned land. Verify lender policy.

questions.question: Is the municipal/property tax being paid regularly?
questions.description:
💰 Municipal Tax Status
Regular tax payment history proves the property is recognized by the municipal body — an important signal for lenders.

options.label: Yes — paid regularly and up to date
Paid but with gaps or arrears

condition.then: Properties without municipal tax records are difficult to finance. Clearing arrears and obtaining tax receipts is recommended before applying.

questions.question: Are there any unauthorized additions or modifications to the property?
questions.description:
🚧 Unauthorized Additions
Extra floors, room additions, or balcony enclosures without permission are common in older areas. The extent affects lender decisions and valuation.

options.label: Minor additions (balcony enclosure, extra room)
options.helperText: Small changes that don't alter the building footprint significantly

condition.then: Major unauthorized construction significantly reduces lender options. Banks will likely reject; select NBFCs may consider at lower LTV and higher rates.

questions.question: What is the status of revenue records for this property?
questions.description:
📑 Revenue Records
Revenue records (7/12 extract in Maharashtra, Khata in Karnataka, Patta in Tamil Nadu, Jamabandi in Rajasthan/Punjab) are the primary proof of land ownership in village/panchayat areas.

options.label: Available and up to date
options.helperText: 7/12, Khata, Patta, RTC — whichever applies in your state

options.label: Available but not updated recently
options.helperText: Records exist but mutation or name transfer pending

condition.then: Properties without revenue records are extremely difficult to finance. Even specialized NBFCs require some form of ownership documentation.

questions.question: Has this colony/layout been regularized by the government?
questions.description:
🏘️ Colony Regularization
Many villages and panchayat areas have colonies that were developed informally but later regularized by state government orders. Regularized colonies are accepted by more lenders.

questions.question: Has the Gram Panchayat issued permission for this construction?
questions.description:
🏡 Gram Panchayat Permission
In panchayat areas, the Gram Panchayat is the local authority that grants building permission. This serves as proof of authorized construction.

questions.question: How did the current owner(s) acquire this property?
questions.description:
📜 Acquisition Method
GPA (Power of Attorney) transfers are rejected by most lenders after the Supreme Court ruling. Inherited properties need succession documents.

condition.then: GPA transfers are not legally valid sales (Supreme Court ruling). Most lenders will reject. Only specialized HFCs may consider at very high rates.
Inherited properties need succession certificate / legal heir certificate / probate. All legal heirs must be co-applicants or provide NOC.

questions.question: Is this property inherited? If so, is the succession properly documented?
questions.description:
🏠 Succession Status
For inherited properties, lenders require succession certificate, legal heir certificate, probate of will, or partition deed — depending on how the property was inherited.

options.label: Inherited — succession documents complete
options.helperText: Succession certificate, will probate, or mutation done

condition.then: Incomplete succession documentation will delay or prevent loan processing. Succession certificate or mutation must be completed first.

questions.question: Are the original property documents available?
questions.description:
📚 Original Documents
Lender holds original documents as mortgage security. Without originals, no lender can process LAP.

condition.then: Original property documents are mandatory for mortgage creation. Without originals, no lender can process LAP.

questions.question: Is the ownership chain (title chain) complete and traceable?
questions.description:
🔗 Title Chain
Lenders need an unbroken chain of ownership from original allotment/sale to current owner.

questions.question: Is there any existing loan / mortgage on this property?
questions.description:
🏦 Existing Mortgage
If property already has a loan, this becomes a Balance Transfer case.

options.label: No — property is free from any loan
Yes — existing mortgage on this property

questions.question: Is the property free from any legal disputes or litigation?

condition.then: Properties under active litigation are rejected by ALL lenders. Dispute must be resolved first.

questions.question: Has an Encumbrance Certificate (EC) been obtained?
questions.description:
📜 Encumbrance Certificate
EC from sub-registrar shows 13-30 year transaction history. Clean EC confirms no hidden claims.

questions.question: What is the current occupation status of the property?
Monthly rental income from this property
What type of rental agreement is in place?
questions.description:
📝 Rental Agreement
Registered lease agreements are accepted as bankable income. Unregistered agreements may not be counted.

condition.then: Without a registered lease, most lenders will not count rental income towards repayment capacity.

switch.then: What is the outstanding principal amount?
What is the outstanding principal of the current loan (LAP), as on today?

questions.description:
💰 Outstanding Principal Amount
This is the remaining loan amount you still owe to your current lender (excluding interest).
Original Loan ₹50,00,000
Principal Paid - ₹15,00,000
Outstanding Principal = ₹35,00,000
⚠️ Common Mistake: Don't confuse this with total remaining EMIs (which includes future interest). Outstanding principal is just the principal portion left.
💡 Where to find it:
  • 📄 Loan Statement from your bank
  • 📄 Schedule of Repayment document
  • 📞 Call your current lender's customer care
  • 💻 Check your net banking/app

condition.then: Please enter a minimum principal outstanding amount of 5 lakh.
Enter a valid amount

questions.question: What's the current interest rate with existing Lender?

condition.then: Interest rate must be between 1% to 40%. Any figure beyond this may be unreasonable to our AI.

questions.question: What's the remaining tenure to close the loan at existing Lender?(in Months)

condition.then: Remaining tenure must be between 12 months (1 year) to 180 months (15 years) as remaining tenures. Any figure beyond this seems unreasonable.

questions.question: How long have you had this loan with your current lender?
questions.description:
⏱️ Loan Vintage
Most lenders require a minimum of 12 months of repayment history before accepting a balance transfer.
Why this matters: Longer repayment history demonstrates financial discipline and improves your chances of getting better terms from the new lender.
💡 Tip: Count from the first EMI payment date, not from the loan sanction date.

condition.then: Most lenders require at least 12 months of repayment history for balance transfer. Very few lenders may accept loans less than 6 months old.
Some lenders require a minimum 12-month relationship. Limited options may be available for loans with 6-12 months vintage.

questions.question: Have all EMIs been paid on time in the last 12 months? (No bounces or delays)
questions.description:
✅ Repayment Track Record
Lenders check your repayment discipline before accepting a balance transfer. A clean track record gets you better rates and higher chances of approval.
What counts as irregular:
  • EMI bounce (cheque/NACH return)
  • Payment delayed beyond due date
  • Partial payment made instead of full EMI
💡 Tip: Check your bank statement or loan account statement for EMI payment history over the last 12 months.

options.label: Yes, all EMIs paid on time

condition.then: 1-2 irregular payments may limit your options. Some NBFCs are flexible on minor irregularities if recent months show improvement.
Frequent EMI bounces significantly reduce balance transfer options. Very few lenders may consider your application, and terms may be less favorable.

What's the current EMI?

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the additional funds (top-up)?
questions.description:
🎯 Top-Up Purpose
Lenders are required to document the purpose of the additional funds as part of regulatory compliance.
💡 Tip: Choose the option that best describes your primary use of the top-up amount.

questions.question: Please specify the required Top-up amount?
questions.description:
💵 Top-Up Loan Amount
A top-up is additional loan amount over and above your existing outstanding principal.
Property Value ₹1,00,00,000
Max LTV (65%) ₹65,00,000
Outstanding Principal - ₹35,00,000
Possible Top-Up = ₹30,00,000
📋 Top-Up Eligibility Factors:
  • Current property market value
  • Your repayment track record
  • Income & existing obligations
  • Lender's LTV policy
💡 Tip: Top-up amounts vary by lender. We'll show you the best available options based on your profile.

condition.then: Lenders do not accept loan applications below 5 lakh. You should try for personal loan / Business loan for such low amount.
Top-up amount should be less than property value.

The loan term determines how long you'll take to repay your Loan Against Property.
Example: ₹50 Lakh LAP @ 10%

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of this loan?
questions.description:
🎯 Loan Purpose
Lenders are required to document the purpose of the loan as part of RBI regulatory compliance.
This helps in:
  • Matching you with the right lender programs
  • Faster processing as purpose is pre-documented
  • Some lenders offer better rates for business use cases
💡 Tip: Choose the option that best describes your primary use of the funds. If you have multiple purposes, select the one for which the majority of the amount will be used.

questions.question: What is your expected average monthly withdrawal from this overdraft facility? (Optional)
questions.description:
💳 Expected Monthly Utilization
For Drop-line OD, you only pay interest on the amount you actually use. Estimating monthly usage helps size the facility correctly.
How DOD works:
  • Sanctioned limit reduces over time (drop-line)
  • Withdraw any amount up to the available limit
  • Pay interest only on the utilized amount
  • Repay and re-use within the available limit
💡 Tip: This is optional but helps lenders offer better terms. If unsure, you can leave this blank.
